questions.q: What is a dictionary entry in ServiceNow, precisely?
options: A description of a field, separate from the field itself
The field itself — a `sys_dictionary` record that defines the field's name, type, and behavior
A cached copy of a database column that the platform ignores at runtime
A backup of a field's values, used only for recovery
questions.explain: There is no separate schema file — the sys_dictionary record IS the field. The platform reads it live on every render.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT an attribute you'd find on a dictionary entry?
options: Max length
Default value
Mandatory flag
The name of the admin who last logged in
questions.explain: Table, column name, label, type, max length, default value, and flags like Mandatory/Read-only/Active/Unique are dictionary attributes. Login history isn't.

questions.q: You check the Mandatory flag on a dictionary entry and save it. What happens next, and why?
options: Nothing, until a developer deploys a validation rule
Only the form you were looking at when you made the change is affected
Every form built against that table immediately requires the field, because the platform reads sys_dictionary live
The change only applies after the next instance upgrade
questions.explain: This is what "metadata-driven" means: behavior changes platform-wide, instantly, because the platform reads the dictionary live. No code ships.

questions.q: What is the fastest way to reach a dictionary entry when you're already looking at the field on an open form?
options: Navigate to System Definition > Dictionary and search by table name
Open System Properties and search for the field name
Right-click the field's label and choose Personalize Dictionary (or Configure > Dictionary)
There is no contextual shortcut; System Definition > Dictionary is the only path
questions.explain: Personalize Dictionary jumps straight from the form to that exact field's dictionary entry, skipping the search.

questions.q: Why does this lesson call the dictionary "the foundation for the rest of the chapter"?
options: Because field types, choice lists, and the lab are all just configuration inside a dictionary entry
Because the dictionary has nothing to do with field types or choice lists
Because later lessons replace the dictionary with a different mechanism
Because only Chapter 4's lab lesson actually uses sys_dictionary
questions.explain: Field type is a dictionary attribute, a choice list is extra data tied to a Choice-type dictionary entry, and the lab is filling in a dictionary entry by hand.
